rules.text: Every hook path exits 0.

question.instructions: Does this change add a hook code path that can exit with a nonzero code or let an exception escape uncaught: process.exit(1), process.exitCode = 1, a throw with no surrounding catch, a rejected promise left unhandled?

rules.text: Every hook path bounds its own time.

question.instructions: Does this change add a network call, subprocess, or wait in a hook with no timeout, AbortSignal, or deadline that bounds how long it can run?

rules.text: Writes nothing to stdout but the JSON the host expects.

question.instructions: Does this change make a hook write to stdout anything other than the final JSON response: console.log, process.stdout.write of progress text, a debug print?

rules.text: No secrets in this repo, ever.

check.how: secret scanner (gitleaks) or grep for key-shaped literals

rules.text: Never accept it [the API key] as a flag — a flag lands in shell history and in CI logs.

question.instructions: Does this change add a command-line flag or argument that takes an API key, token, or secret value?

rules.text: Never log it [the API key].

question.instructions: Does this change write an API key, token, auth header, or the env object holding them to a log, console, error message, or output?

rules.text: ~/.oh-my-plumb/.env ... is the only file oh-my-plumb may ever write a key to.

question.instructions: Does this change write an API key or token to any file other than ~/.oh-my-plumb/.env, or write that file without owner-only permissions (mode 0o600)?

rules.text: Verify before claiming done: tests green, pnpm build + typecheck clean, and the end-to-end path exercised against live Jev.

check.reason: about the process before finishing, not the code

rules.text: No AI attribution in commits or pull requests.

check.reason: lives in commit messages and PR text, which edits do not show

rules.text: Pass user-facing words through the humanizer before shipping them.

check.reason: about a process step, not something visible in a diff

rules.text: State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.

check.reason: about the conversation, not the code

rules.text: If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.

check.reason: about the conversation, not the code

rules.text: If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.

check.reason: about the conversation, not the code

rules.text: If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

check.reason: about the conversation, not the code

rules.text: No features beyond what was asked.

question.instructions: Does this change add a feature, command, option, or file that is unrelated to the main purpose the rest of the change serves?

rules.text: No abstractions for single-use code.

question.instructions: Does this change add a new function, class, type, or module that has exactly one caller or one implementation and only wraps or forwards to other code?

criteria.true: a new makeClient() used once that just calls new Client(opts)
criteria.false: a helper called from three places

rules.text: No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.

question.instructions: Does this change add parameters, options, env vars, or config fields that every caller in the change passes the same value to, or that nothing sets?

rules.text: No error handling for impossible scenarios.

question.instructions: Does this change add a check, try/catch, or fallback for a case the surrounding types or control flow already rule out: a null check on a non-nullable value, a catch around code that cannot throw, a default for an exhaustive switch already covered?

rules.text: If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

question.instructions: How long is this change compared with the shortest code that would do the same thing?
criteria: as short as it can be

rules.text: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

question.instructions: Would a senior engineer reviewing this change say it is overcomplicated: layers of indirection, generic machinery, or state that a direct version would not need?

rules.text: Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.

question.instructions: Does this change reword comments, reformat, or rename in lines unrelated to the change's main purpose?

rules.text: Preserve intentional blank lines between methods and logical blocks. Do not compact whitespace to reduce line count.

question.instructions: Among the removed lines, is there at least one blank line separating methods or logical blocks that was deleted without the surrounding code otherwise changing?

rules.text: Don't refactor things that aren't broken.

question.instructions: Does this change restructure existing working code (move, split, merge, rewrite functions) in a way the change's main purpose does not require?

rules.text: Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.

check.reason: needs the rest of the file or repository to know the existing style

rules.text: If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

question.instructions: Does this change delete functions, exports, or files that the rest of the change never touched or referenced?

rules.text: Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

check.reason: 'unless asked' depends on the conversation; the diff side is covered by delete-unrelated-dead-code

rules.text: Transform tasks into verifiable goals.

check.reason: about how the agent plans, not the code

rules.text: "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"

question.instructions: Does this change add input validation or parsing rules without adding or changing any test file?

criteria.true: a new zod refine in src/ and no *.test.ts touched
criteria.false: a new zod refine plus a test feeding it invalid input

rules.text: "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"

question.instructions: Does this change fix incorrect behaviour in source code without adding or changing any test file?

rules.text: "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

check.reason: about running tests, not the code

rules.text: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan.

check.reason: about the conversation, not the code

rules.text: Default to no comment.

question.instructions: How many comments do the added lines contain?
criteria: several comments, or a multi-line block

rules.text: Don't narrate what the code does — the reader sees the map, the switch, the names.

question.instructions: Among the added lines, is there at least one comment whose content a reader could reconstruct from the code directly next to it?

criteria.true:
// loop over rules and check each one
for (const rule of rules) check(rule)
criteria.false:
// hosts kill hooks after 5s, so stay under it
const DEADLINE_MS = 4000

rules.text: Comment only the non-obvious: a reason, a gotcha, a workaround, a constraint, a "looks wrong but isn't."

question.instructions: Among the added lines, is there a comment that gives no reason, gotcha, workaround, or constraint — only a label, a section header, or a description?

rules.text: If code needs a comment to be understood, first make the code clearer (rename, extract).

question.instructions: Does this change add a comment that explains what a variable, function, or expression means, where a clearer name or an extracted function would say the same thing?

rules.text: Delete comments that restate the adjacent line.

check.reason: asks to remove comments that already exist; a diff of new lines cannot show what was left in place

rules.text: Every comment must earn its place: if you can't name what it tells the reader that the code doesn't, drop it.

check.reason: a self-test for the author; the diff side is covered by comment-without-why

rules.text: Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding compatibility layers, fallbacks, or migrations.

question.instructions: Does this change add code whose only job is to keep an old shape or behavior working: a deprecated alias, a legacy-format fallback, a shim, or a migration from an older format?

criteria.true: const cfg = parsed.rules ?? parsed.legacyRules // support old files
criteria.false: renaming a field and updating every reader

rules.text: Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirements. Avoid speculative abstractions, configuration, and indirection.

question.instructions: Does this change add a layer of indirection (registry, factory, adapter, plugin hook, strategy map) that currently has only one implementation behind it?

criteria.true: a providers map with one entry, looked up by name

rules.text: Grow the system in layers. Never trade a working product for unfinished complexity.

question.instructions: Does this change leave half-built code in the product path: a stub that throws 'not implemented', an unwired module, or a branch that replaces working behavior with something incomplete?

rules.text: Keep components modular and concerns clearly separated.

check.reason: needs the module layout of the rest of the repository

rules.text: Prefer established, well-maintained libraries when they reduce overall complexity or improve reliability. Do not reimplement common functionality without a clear reason.

question.instructions: Does this change hand-write common functionality a well-known library provides: a retry or backoff loop, debounce, deep clone or deep equal, glob matching, argument parsing, semver comparison, or a schema validator?

rules.text: Lean on the dependencies already in the project before writing your own implementation or adding packages.

check.reason: needs the project's installed dependencies and their APIs

rules.text: Make architectural decisions for the long term. Do not accept a stopgap that only works for now and is meant to be replaced later.

question.instructions: Does this change add code that says it is temporary: a TODO, FIXME or HACK to replace it later, or a comment or name saying 'for now', 'temporary', 'quick fix' or 'workaround until'?

criteria.true: // TODO: replace with real cache, in-memory for now
criteria.false: a comment explaining why a timeout is 800 ms

rules.text: Highly prefer E2E tests as the sole testing mechanism. Use them to verify complex features work.

question.instructions: Does this change add a test that mocks or stubs the project's own modules (vi.mock, jest.mock, spyOn on an internal function) instead of running the real code path end to end?

rules.text: At the end of E2E tests, produce a verifiable and repeatable artifact.

check.reason: needs the whole test harness to see whether an artifact is produced

rules.text: If you must test a system in isolation, FIRST write all the ways it could fail, THEN write the code.

check.reason: about the order of work, not the code

rules.text: Never use if/else-if chains for mutually-exclusive variants.

question.instructions: Does this change add an if / else-if chain that branches on the discriminant (type, kind, status, code) of a union or enum instead of a switch?

rules.text: Closed sets use an exhaustive switch + assertNever ... end with default: return assertNever(value).

question.instructions: Does this change add a switch over a union or enum discriminant whose default branch is missing or does something other than call assertNever?

rules.text: When behavior depends on several related status checks, derive one closed decision/status type and switch over that — don't scatter conditionals through a method.

question.instructions: Does this change add three or more separate if-conditions in one function that test related status flags, instead of deriving one status value and switching on it?

rules.text: Define assertNever once in the schema package's utils and import it everywhere.

check.how: no-restricted-syntax on a declaration named assertNever outside packages/schema

rules.text: Use type, not interface.
Discriminated unions for state — every multi-shape value carries a type/kind discriminant. No optional-field soup where one shape is meant.

question.instructions: Does this change add a type with two or more optional fields that are meant to be set in different situations, with no type or kind field saying which shape it is?

criteria.true: type Check = { pattern?: string; question?: Question; reason?: string }
criteria.false: type Check = { type: 'lint'; pattern: string } | { type: 'model'; question: Question }

rules.text: No type casting. as is a bug until proven otherwise. (as const and zod .parse() outputs are fine.)
Expected failures use typed domain errors with a stable machine-readable code (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE) callers can switch on exhaustively.

question.instructions: Among the added lines, is there a `throw new Error(` or `new Error(` whose message describes an expected failure such as a missing file, bad input, or refused request?

rules.text: Concise messages, no terminal punctuation.

check.how: no-restricted-syntax on Error message literals ending in . or !

rules.text: Deterministic ID/key formats have a single owner: one named creation function per format. Never inline-format the same ID in two places.

check.reason: needs the rest of the repository to know whether the format already has an owner

rules.text: Anything crossing a process/API boundary is zod-parsed at the edge.

question.instructions: Does this change use data from JSON.parse, a fetch response, stdin, a file read, or process.env without passing it through a zod schema .parse / .safeParse first?

rules.text: Internal code trusts parsed types, never re-validates ad hoc.

check.reason: needs to know whether the value was already parsed upstream

rules.text: Zero Coldtea dependency. Nothing here may require Coldtea to be installed, running, or reachable.
Every verdict must trace to a named rule a person can read and rewrite.

question.instructions: Does this change produce or report a verdict, finding, or violation that does not carry the id of the rule it came from?

rules.text: No default rules. Rules come only from the user's own instruction files.

question.instructions: Does this change add a hardcoded rule definition to the tool's source: a literal object or array with a rule id and rule text or question, used when the user's rubric does not supply it?

criteria.true: const DEFAULT_RULES = [{ id: 'no-console', text: 'Do not use console.log' }]
criteria.false: reading rules from the parsed rubric.json

rules.text: Band verdicts, never threshold at 0.5. Act above a high score, flag the middle, ignore below.

question.instructions: Does this change turn a model score into a verdict with a single cut-off (such as >= 0.5) instead of separate high and low bands with a middle band for the human?

rules.text: Trim instructions for tokens as well as for readability, and use scope globs to keep out-of-scope questions out of the request entirely.

check.reason: guidance for writing rubric text, not code

rules.text: A rule a linter can enforce exactly, for free, must never be sent to a model.

question.instructions: Does this change send rules whose check type is lint, deferred, or unenforceable into a model or judge request?
